explication:
<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose  
   • This is a single-page application (SPA) front-end for Stremio (“Stremio-Web”), built with React, TypeScript/JavaScript, Less, and bundled by Webpack.  
   • It provides a media-center UI to discover, watch and organize video content via third-party addons and streaming servers.  

2. File Structure Analysis  
   • Top level contains Dockerfile, http_server.js, webpack.config.js, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, CI workflows (.github), and static asset folders (favicons, fonts, images, screenshots).  
   • src/ subdivides into:  
     – common/: shared hooks, utilities, constants, styling (Less).  
     – components/: reusable React UI components (buttons, modals, inputs, navigation bars, video placeholders, etc.).  
     – router/: a client-side router implementation and contexts for modals & route focus.  
     – routes/: page-level React modules (Board, Discover, Library, Player, Settings, etc.) organized by feature; each route has its own styles, hooks, and subcomponents.  
     – services/: integration layer that abstracts communication with external systems (CoreTransport for the local Stremio Core, ShellTransport for Electron shell, ChromecastTransport, WebTorrent streaming). It also supplies a ServicesContext provider.  
     – types/: TypeScript type definitions.  
   • Configuration files include tsconfig.json, eslint.config.mjs, .gitignore, and CI workflows in .github/workflows.

3. README Insights  
   • Describes how to install dependencies (pnpm), run the dev server, build for production, or run the static build in Docker on port 8080.  
   • No backend code is included—this repo produces static assets served via http_server.js or any static file host (e.g., GitHub Pages).  

4. How to Draw the System Design Diagram  
   a. Identify Main Components  
      – Static Asset Host: HTTP server (http_server.js or any static-file server, Docker container).  
      – Browser / React App: the user’s web browser running the compiled bundle.  
      – React Subsystems within the Browser:  
        • Router Module – handles URL → route mapping, modal contexts, route focus.  
        • UI Component Layer – reusable components and route-specific components in routes/.  
        • ServicesContext – React Context/provider that exposes service APIs to components.  
        • Common Utilities – custom hooks, constants, animations, theming.  
      – External Services & Integrations:  
        • Local Stremio Core service (JSON-RPC over WebSocket/HTTP) via CoreTransport.  
        • Native shell (Electron) via ShellTransport.  
        • Chromecast devices via ChromecastTransport.  
        • Streaming servers and WebTorrent P2P network (HTTP/WebSocket & WebTorrent API).  
        • Third-party addon cloud services for metadata and catalogs.  

   b. Relationships and Interactions  
      – The HTTP server delivers static JS/CSS/HTML to the browser.  
      – Browser loads the React bundle and initializes the App.  
      – Router renders the correct route component based on the URL.  
      – UI Components call hooks (from common/) to read state or dispatch actions.  
      – ServicesContext wraps the component tree and provides transports (Core, Shell, Chromecast) and streaming hooks (useStreamingServer, useTorrent).  
      – Transports communicate asynchronously with external endpoints (local core, shell, Chromecast, streaming server, addon endpoints).  
      – Player route uses HTML5 Video element to render streams acquired via streaming server URL or WebTorrent.  

   c. Architectural Patterns  
      – Component-based UI (React).  
      – Unidirectional data flow via React Context & custom hooks.  
      – Client-side routing (custom Router).  
      – Separation of concerns: UI vs. routing vs. integration/services vs. utility logic.  
      – Build Pipelines: Webpack bundles assets; Docker image packs static server.  

   d. Technologies & Frameworks  
      – React, React Context, custom Router (no React-Router).  
      – TypeScript + JavaScript (JSX/TSX).  
      – Less for styling.  
      – Webpack for bundling.  
      – http_server.js or any static file host for serving assets.  
      – Node.js (dev dependencies, Docker base).  
      – pnpm as package manager.  
      – WebTorrent for P2P streaming.  
      – JSON-RPC transports for core/shell communication.  

5. Diagram-Tailoring Guidelines for this SPA  
   • Emphasize the separation between the static server (or CDN) and the browser’s React application.  
   • Within the browser, clearly delineate:  
     – Router & route contexts  
     – UI component hierarchy (components/ vs. routes/)  
     – ServicesContext & transport layers  
     – Common utilities/hooks layer  
   • Show external systems: local Core, Electron shell, Chromecast devices, streaming servers/P2P network, and addon endpoints.  

6. Mandatory Diagram Elements  
   • Label each box: e.g., “Static Asset Server,” “Browser,” “React Router,” “UI Components,” “ServicesContext,” “CoreTransport,” etc.  
   • Use directional arrows to indicate:  
     – Asset flow (Server → Browser)  
     – Data flow (UI → ServicesContext → Transports → External Services)  
     – Event or callback flows (Transports → UI via hooks/context)  
   • Apply color coding or shapes:  
     – One color/shape for in-browser modules (React layers).  
     – Another for external services.  
     – Another for infrastructure (HTTP server, Docker).  

7. Detail Emphasis  
   • Capture each logical layer and integration point.  
   • Drill down to highlight the React Context/provider pattern and custom hooks as the bridge between UI and transports.  
   • Don’t omit any major transport or service: Core, Shell, Chromecast, Streaming Server, WebTorrent, Addons.  
   • Represent page-level routes (Board, Discover, Player, etc.) as sub-modules under the Router or UI layer to show feature segmentation.  
   • Keep your diagram organized top-down (Infrastructure → Browser Shell → Application Layers → External Systems).  

This structured diagram will give a clear, accurate, and detailed architectural view of Stremio-Web’s front-end system.  
</explanation>
